we developed a new method to measure the gas response of materials that are suitable for implementation in FET-based gas sensors.

the proposed technique allows to measure the surface charge density induced by adsorbed gas species on the sensing material, and the sensitivity of platinum to hydrogen diluted in air was evaluated in the temperature range 80–190 °C at a constant hydrogen concentration of 4 and 0.5–4 % at a temperature of 130 °C.
we developed a novel technique to measure the charge induced by gas adsorption on the surface of materials for implementation as FET gas sensors.

the study of the gas sensitivity of Pt to H2 in the temperature range of 80 to 200 °C, with a view to its use as a sensing element in a FET-based gas sensor.
the development of novel gas sensors for the detection of hydrogen and other combustible gases in air.
the development of novel techniques and methodologies to investigate and characterize materials and devices for gas sensing applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charge measurement is able to detect the gas sensitivity of the material and that the sensitivity is a function of the temperature and the gas concentration.
the proposed charge measurement is a very promising approach to investigate gas sensing materials for FET-based gas sensors.
the proposed charge measurement approach is a novel and powerful tool for the gas sensitivity investigation and optimization of materials for FET-based gas sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel method to characterize the gas sensitivity of a material for use in a field-effect gas sensor.

we have developed a new technique for the characterization of materials suitable for implementation in gas sensor devices and that we have demonstrated its applicability for the evaluation of platinum sensitivity to hydrogen diluted synthetic air.
the proposed technique is a powerful and reliable method for the characterization of gas-sensitive materials for implementation in FET-based gas sensors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gas sensitivity of a given material can be evaluated by means of the charge measurement technique, which is based on the surface charge induced on a material exposed to the gas species under investigation.

the gas sensitivity characterization technique based on the measurement the surface charge induced on the material is a very promising approach for the investigation of the gas sensing properties of materials, especially for the development of field effect transistor gas sensors.
the proposed technique is suitable for the characterization of the gas sensitivity of metal-oxide-based gas sensors.
